text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 4 in history:
1190 - Richard I of England and Philip II of France started on the Third Crusade.
1631 - The world's first employment agency opened in Paris.
1753 - John Pierre Blanchard, French balloonist, born. In 1785, he became the first to cross the English Channel by balloon.
1776 - The American Declaration of Independence was signed.
1799 - Oscar I, king of Sweden and Norway (1844-59), born in Paris. He pursued a policy of Swedish neutrality and Scandinavian unity.
1804 - Nathaniel Hawthorne, U.S. novelist and short-story writer, born. One of the first major U.S. novelists, his most famous works are "The Scarlet Letter" and "The House of the Seven Gables".
1807 - Giuseppe Garibaldi, Italian military leader and central figure in the struggle for Italian unity, born.
1826 - Thomas Jefferson, third U.S. president (1801-09), and John Adams, second president (1797-1801), both died on this day.
1831 - James Monroe, fifth U.S. president (1817-25), died. In 1823 he introduced the Monroe Doctrine, which committed the U.S. to a Western Hemisphere safe from aggression.
1845 - Thomas John Barnardo, Dublin-born philanthropist, born. In 1870 he founded the first of the "Dr. Barnardo's Homes" for destitute boys in London.
1847 - James Anthony Bailey, U.S. circus impresario, born. In partnership with Phineas Barnum, he made the American circus the most successful ever.
1848 - The Communist Manifesto, written by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, was published.
1863 - In the U.S. Civil War, Confederates defeated by Union forces at the Battle of Vicksburg.
1872 - Calvin Coolidge, 30th president of the United States (1923-29), born. His term as president was marked by increasing economic prosperity and an absence of crises.
1884 - Statue of Liberty was presented to America by the people of France.
1885 - Louis B. Mayer, U.S. film producer, born in Russia. Along with with Samuel Goldwyn, he formed the MGM studios and guided it through the "golden age" of cinema in the U.S.
1900 - Louis "Satchmo" Armstrong, legendary U.S. jazz musician born. Appeared in many films as an entertainer and musician notably "Cabin in the Sky" and "High Society".
1903 - First Pacific telegraph cable, between San Francisco and Manila, went into operation.
1904 - Construction of the Panama Canal began.
1927 - Gina Lollobrigida, Italian actress, born. She became a star in films from the 1940s, notably in "Beat the Devil" and "Solomon and Sheba".
1927 - Neil Simon, U.S. playwright and screenwriter, born. His hits included "Barefoot in the Park" and the "Sunshine Boys".
1934 - Marie Curie, Polish-French physicist and Nobel prize winner, died.
1943 - Wladyslaw Sikorski, Polish statesman and prime minister, was killed in an air crash. He led Poland's government in exile during World War Two.
1946 - Philippines gained independence from America.
1976 - Israel launched commando raid on Entebbe airport in Uganda to rescue 102 hostages held by Arab and West German hijackers of Air France plane.
1979 - Former Algerian president Ahmed Ben Bella was released after 14 years detention. Ben Bella, Algeria's first president, was overthrown in a 1965 coup and had been kept under arrest ever since.
1991 - Former Soviet foreign minister Eduard Shevardnazde decided to leave the Communist Party.
1994 - French President Francois Mitterrand, became the first foreigner to address South Africa's new parliament.
